The `gws` CLI (`/opt/homebrew/bin/gws`, personal account eric.rash11@gmail.com) can
create and fully populate Google Forms even though **no `forms.body` scope is
granted**. The 12 granted scopes include `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive`,
and that is sufficient for both `forms forms create` and `forms forms batchUpdate`.

**Why:** worth recording because the Contacts API on this same auth returns 403 for a
missing scope (see [[fireflies-cli-broken-on-mac]] for the sibling env traps), so the
reasonable expectation is that Forms would fail too. It doesn't. Don't skip Forms work
on a scope assumption — try it.

**How to apply:**

- `gws forms forms create --json '{"info":{"title":"...","documentTitle":"..."}}'`
  accepts **title only**. The API rejects description, items, and settings on create.
- Everything else goes through `forms forms batchUpdate` with a `requests` array:
  `updateFormInfo` (with `updateMask`) for the description, then `createItem` with an
  incrementing `location.index` per question.
- Item shapes: `questionItem.question.textQuestion{paragraph:bool}`,
  `...choiceQuestion{type: RADIO|CHECKBOX|DROP_DOWN, options:[{value}]}`,
  and `pageBreakItem` for a section.
- Editing an existing question needs `updateItem` with the item's `itemId`, the
  question's `questionId`, `location.index`, **and** an `updateMask` such as
  `questionItem.question.choiceQuestion.options`. Omitting itemId/questionId appends a
  duplicate instead of editing in place.
- `--dry-run` validates locally before sending. Use it; batchUpdate is not idempotent
  and a re-run duplicates every item.
- New forms are created **published and accepting responses**. On a personal account
  that is a loose end — unpublish or delete after use.
- Gmail drafts work the same way via `gmail users drafts create/update` with a
  base64url RFC822 `message.raw`. Passing an existing draft `id` to `update` edits in
  place rather than creating a duplicate.

`claude -p "..." --disallowedTools Bash` does **not** stop shell execution. The
context-mode plugin's MCP tools (`ctx_execute`, `ctx_batch_execute`,
`ctx_execute_file`) run shell commands and are not covered by denying `Bash`.
Seen 2026-09-12: a headless "audit my AI OS" smoke test with Bash denied still
ran `aios-metrics.py` through the MCP shell.

**Why:** a smoke test believed to be read-only can run, and in principle write,
anything the MCP shell can.

**How to apply:** for a truly read-only headless run, also deny the
`mcp__plugin_context-mode_context-mode__*` tools (or disable the plugin). Then
check for side effects afterwards (git status, memory dirs). Never report a headless
run as "no side effects possible" on the Bash deny alone.

Kenny Boyd (reviewer on the Baylor Athletics Software and Technology Management

others"). Acks are one line ("Received. Thank you"). Credits people by name, often
including partner offices ("would not have been possible without…"). Tailors one

### DEV/project_keystoneos-verification-habits.md

---
name: keystoneos-verification-habits
description: "Where KeystoneOS state claims are authoritative vs misleading, and which readings have already produced wrong conclusions"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: ea41d487-7812-4180-a6a8-f76a99753f83
  modified: 2026-10-24T14:52:01.495Z
---

This system is well-instrumented, which makes its few misleading surfaces
dangerous — they look authoritative. Check these before drawing conclusions.

**"Did a job run today?"** Only `KeystoneOS Morning` runs through `run-job.ps1`;
AgySync, DailyBackup, MsysKeepAlive, Reconcile, Rituals and StackDoctor invoke
their scripts directly and write **no ledger row**. So `outputs/run-ledger.json`
under-reports. Correctness is fine — `Test-JobCompleteOn` checks the ledger *or*
the job's `successProbe`. Ask `.\scripts\keystone-reconcile.ps1 -DryRun -Json`,
never the ledger alone and never `Get-ScheduledTaskInfo`.

**memsearch timeout streaks are not failures.** The SessionEnd hook
(`~/.claude/hooks/memsearch-sync.js`) is deliberately best-effort. Since 2026-09-02
it hands the index to a detached worker and returns at once, so the `timeout: 50`
still in `~/.claude/settings.json` no longer bounds the index; see
[[memsearch-hook-timeout-cap]]. The daily backup's uncapped full reindex absorbs
backlog and resets the counter. Since 2026-10-22 that backup runs hourly
12:00-17:00 on AC power, so a streak clears by afternoon; see [[backup-sync-system]].
(Superseded 2026-10-24: the nightly ran 00:30, then 09:00 from 2026-08-29.) A streak of 16 on 2026-07-28 was
read as a broken indexer and produced a whole plan step to "fix" it — the nightly
cleared it the same night, exactly as designed. Alarm threshold is 6.

**A scheduler's exit code is not the job's outcome.** It reports the last
*scheduled* run, so a green log and a red status routinely coexist: a manual or
out-of-band run never clears it, and a sleep/wake kill mid-run sets it while the
day's work still completed on a later retry. Read the job's own log for a
same-day clean end before treating a red status as rot. Two recorded instances:
the Windows sleep-kill exit on `KeystoneOS-DailyBackup` (2026-08-01, details in
[[backup-task-sleepkill-signature]]), and `launchctl list` on 2026-08-31 still
showing the failed 09:00 `com.keystone.dailybackup` after the corrected re-run
completed with 0 errors. Both cleared themselves at the next scheduled run; a
forced re-run would have been cosmetic. (Generalised from that Windows-only
memory. It was archived to `_archive/` on 2026-09-01, came back as a live copy in
the 2026-09-24 Windows memory mirror, and is kept unindexed as Windows history.)

**The test suite is main-checkout-only.** `Get-KeystoneDevRoot` resolves the DEV
root as `<repoRoot>\..`, which from a worktree yields
`KeystoneOS\.claude\worktrees\`. `tests\keystone-reconcile.ps1` therefore always
throws in a worktree. Baseline on main is 23 pass / 1 fail
(`skill-verification-contracts.ps1`, unrelated). Always baseline against main
before blaming a change.

**Three claims failed verification in one session (2026-07-28/29):** that the
registry pointed at a stale clone, that the reconciler was wasting hours on
redundant backups, and that the indexer was chronically broken. All three were
plausible from a point-in-time reading and all three were wrong. State a claim
about this system only after re-running the check that produces it.

**`canonicalPath` in `data/projects.json` must be a real filesystem path — never a URL.**
Learned the hard way 2026-08-15: retiring a project, I set it to the GitHub URL so the field
would not point at a deleted directory. That took down the entire 06:00 morning cadence at
the dashboard step. `Join-Path`, `Get-Item`, `Resolve-Path`, `Get-ChildItem` and
`Convert-Path` all throw *"Cannot find drive. A drive with the name 'https' does not exist"*
on a URL. **`Test-Path` is the trap: it returns `False` on a URL instead of throwing**, which
is exactly why the `if (-not (Test-Path $Path))` guards in `Get-PathSummary` and
`Get-GitSummary` sail past it and the failure lands somewhere further downstream.

A path that simply *does not exist* is handled cleanly by those guards, so the correct value
for a retired project is its old directory; put the repo URL in a separate field
(`restoreFrom`) that nothing treats as a path.

**Recurrence 2026-09-12 — same class, cross-machine variant: a Windows drive letter.**
The 2026-09-09 GitHub consolidation merge left a **duplicate** `reMarkale_extract` entry in
`data/projects.json` whose `canonicalPath` was `C:\Users\eric_rash\Desktop\DEV\...`. On macOS
that throws *"Cannot find drive. A drive with the name 'C' does not exist"* — identical
mechanism to the URL case, different scheme. It killed morning-cadence on **every run from
2026-09-10 through 2026-09-12** (5 runs), and the failure was **invisible in the usual
places**: `outputs/jobs/morning-cadence-*.{out,err}.log` were both 0 bytes and
`morning-cadence.err` was empty. The only record was `outputs/morning/cadence.log` —
grep it for `cadence FAILED` first, not the job logs. Fixed by deleting the duplicate
(the Mac entry was intact); BOM preserved on the write, see [[settings-json-bom-trap]].

**The asymmetry is the durable lesson: this fault is one-way.** Windows tolerates a
`/Users/...` path (`Test-Path` just returns `False`); macOS *throws* on `C:\` under
`$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"`. So any shared JSON that both machines write will break
the Mac and never the Windows box — and it will recur every time Windows registers a new
project. Expect it after any cross-machine merge; grep shared `data/*.json` for
`eric_rash` or `C:\\` as part of post-merge cleanup. See [[github-consolidation]].

**How to apply:** after editing any `data/*.json` that KeystoneOS scripts consume, run the
consumers before trusting the edit — `scripts/keystone.ps1 dashboard`, `cockpit`, `snapshot`
are quick and cover most path handling. A JSON-validity check proves nothing here; the file
parsed fine and still broke the cadence. See [[morning-briefing-retired]].

### DEV/project_memory-compiler-pipeline.md

---
name: memory-compiler-pipeline
description: How the claude-memory-compiler flush/index pipeline fails and how to tell which stage broke; SessionStart injection was rewritten to a pointer 2026-08-29
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 174cde34-d23d-454b-8db8-9365e7f728f2
  modified: 2026-08-29T20:05:21.521Z
---

The compiler at `~/.claude/claude-memory-compiler/` has three stages. Each fails
differently and the symptoms look alike, so identify the stage before fixing.

**Stage 1 — `hooks/session-end.py`.** Writes `scripts/session-flush-<uuid>-<YYYYMMDD>-<HHMMSS>.md`,
then spawns `flush.py`. Logs every firing to `scripts/flush.log` as `SessionEnd fired`.
If `flush.log` has no such line for days but the hook works when run by hand, sessions
are being *closed* rather than exited cleanly — not a config break. Self-verifying: end
one session normally and re-check the tail.

**Stage 2 — `scripts/flush.py`.** Calls the Agent SDK, appends to `daily/<date>.md`, writes
`scripts/last-flush.json` **only on success**, and **deletes its context file on success**.
Therefore **every leftover `session-flush-*.md` is a flush that died**, and its datestamp
maps to a missing `daily/<date>.md`. That is the cheapest diagnostic in the whole system —
count the leftovers. A stale `last-flush.json` means flushes are *dying*, not that the hook
never fired. Recover one by hand:
`uv run --directory ~/.claude/claude-memory-compiler python scripts/flush.py <context-file> <session-id> [YYYY-MM-DD]`
Success = `Result: FLUSH_OK` + `Flush complete` in `flush.log`.

**The third arg is a backfill date, added 2026-08-29.** Without it `flush.py` always writes
to *today's* log, so recovering old stranded files silently misfiles them under the current
date. Always pass the date parsed from the filename when backfilling; entries are then
marked `(backfilled …)`.

**Batch-recovery trap — the 60-second dedup guard destroys data.** `flush.py` skips a run
whose `session_id` matches `last-flush.json` within 60s, and **deletes the context file on
that skip path too**. One session can have several stranded files (different timestamps), so
a loop that hits the same uuid twice inside a minute silently loses the second one — it still
prints as consumed. Hit 2026-08-29: 12 files ran, 10 flushed, 2 dropped. Before trusting a
batch, check `grep -c "Skipping duplicate flush" flush.log`, and either group runs so repeats
of a uuid are >60s apart or run repeats individually.
Recovery is possible because `~/.claude` is captured to the SSD: the deleted files came back
from `/Volumes/CRASHBOX/AssistantBackup/claude/claude-memory-compiler/scripts/`.

**Stage 3 — memsearch index.** `INDEX full set: Indexed 0 chunks` in the nightly log is
**usually not an indexer fault** — it means nothing new arrived. A dead stage 2 starves it
and looks identical. Check leftovers/`last-flush.json` before suspecting memsearch.
memsearch is a **uv tool**: binary `~/.local/bin/memsearch`, env
`~/.local/share/uv/tools/memsearch/`. Test an import directly with that env's python
(`.../memsearch/bin/python -c "import onnxruntime"`) rather than inferring from index counts.
Reinstall with `uv tool install --force memsearch`, never pip — and re-apply the local flush
patch afterwards, which any reinstall strips.
Superseded 2026-10-24: the Mac `store.py` has no flush patch (the patch was for a Windows
remote Milvus server), and indexing works without it on Milvus Lite (2026-10-24 backup: 2,941
chunks indexed). `uv tool install --force memsearch` strips nothing on the Mac.

**`hooks/session-start.py` — rewritten 2026-08-29.** It used to paste all of
`knowledge/index.md` into every session. That file is ~48k chars against a 20k cap, so the
index was truncated mid-table **and the `## Recent Daily Log` section was pushed off the end
entirely** — the one part that is always relevant never arrived. It now emits a pointer
(article counts + paths + the `memsearch search` command) and always includes the log:
20,039 → 682 chars. If a session needs the index, read
`~/.claude/claude-memory-compiler/knowledge/index.md` on demand. Backups of the pre-change
files are `*.bak-2026-08-29` beside each.

---

`~/.claude/hooks/memsearch-sync.js` (SessionEnd) ran `memsearch index <10 paths>` through
`spawnSync` with a **45s cap**, sized in July against a "~17s fixed floor, ~5s incremental"
measurement. Measured again 2026-09-02 against the current corpus (~1,450 files;
`SecondBrain/Inbox/meetings` alone is 593 and `SecondBrain/Knowledge` 334):

| run | time |
|---|---|
| no-op, nothing new to embed | **33s** (was ~17s) |
| one day of accumulated content | **278s** (232 chunks, ~1s/chunk) |

So the cap left ~12s of embedding budget — under a dozen new chunks. **Every ordinary
session-end index was timing out.** Incremental indexing had quietly degraded to "whatever
the 09:00 nightly full reindex picks up", leaving search up to 24h stale.

**Why it stayed invisible for weeks.** Three dampers stacked:
`daily-backup.ps1` resets `.memsearch-timeout-streak` every morning, the escalation
threshold is 6 consecutive timeouts, and the hook writes only to `.memsearch-index.log`
below that. So a normal day of 2-4 session-ends never reached the threshold and never
surfaced. It took **six session-ends inside 47 minutes** (2026-09-01, 21:09-21:56) to
produce a 7-long streak and one `.errors.log` line. The alarm fired on burst *frequency*,
never on the underlying constant failure.

**The misread that line invites:** ETIMEDOUT + a clustered burst pattern-matches
[[milvus-lock-misdiagnosis]] (session-end lock contention), and the hook's own comments
say exactly that. It was not contention — `pgrep`/`lsof` showed no holder and the DB was
healthy. **Time the actual command before believing the comment.**

**Fix (2026-09-02): detached background worker.** The hook now re-execs itself as
`node memsearch-sync.js --worker` with `detached: true, stdio: 'ignore'` and `.unref()`,
then exits — measured **42ms**. The worker keeps the entire original body, so it owns the
PID lock (clustered session-ends still elect one indexer), writes `INDEX_LOG`, and runs
every error branch. Its `spawnSync` cap was 600s: a runaway guard, not a budget, so an
ETIMEDOUT there genuinely meant ">10 minutes". **Raised to 3h on 2026-10-07** (Windows indexing
under memory pressure ran ~1.2 s/chunk, so 600s runs were killed mid-backlog); the PID lock and
a 30-min cooldown stop overlap. Read the cap in `memsearch-sync.js` before quoting it.

- `stdio: 'ignore'` is **not optional** — inherited or piped stdio keeps the harness's pipe
  open and it waits for the child anyway, rebuilding the timeout with extra steps.
- Self-respawn, **not** an `sh -c` wrapper: the wrapper would discard the lock ownership
  and all four error-classification branches.
- The old header justified staying synchronous with a **Windows** process-group race.
  That rationale died with the 2026-08-05 migration; the comment now says so, because the
  next reader would otherwise "restore" the bug.

**How to apply:**
- A fixed timeout sized against a measured corpus is a **dated** number. When the corpus is
  something that grows every day (the vault, meetings, dailies), the cap has an expiry date
  nobody writes down. Prefer detaching over raising a cap; if a cap must stay, record the
  measurement and the date beside it so drift is visible.
- Never size a SessionEnd hook to block. Session teardown cannot wait minutes, so any
  design where "correct" means minutes must be asynchronous.
- Both harnesses wire their own copy. `~/.codex/hooks/memsearch-sync.js` is now a
  **symlink** to the Claude copy (2026-09-02) so the pair cannot drift again — same fix as
  `~/.codex/AGENTS.md`. Since 2026-10-24 the whole `~/.codex/hooks` folder is a symlink to
  `~/.claude/hooks`, so there is one copy to edit. See [[memsearch-index-path-drift]] for the
  four-copy history.
- Superseded 2026-10-24: `~/DEV/KeystoneOS/scripts/codex-hooks/memsearch-sync.ps1` (a dead 45s
  Windows copy nothing wired) was removed with the other Codex PowerShell hooks.

Related: [[milvus-lock-misdiagnosis]], [[memsearch-index-path-drift]],
[[memory-compiler-pipeline]], [[backup-sync-system]], [[keystoneos-verification-habits]]

**2026-09-22 — a slow nightly index was the Mac sleeping, not memsearch.** The daily backup's
full index took 18 min for 0 new chunks (09-21 09:44) and 15 min for 309 chunks (09-21 18:12).
Timed while awake: no-op ~9s fixed startup, `dev-docs` (763 files) no-op 26s, full set 83s with
79 new chunks (~0.7s/chunk). `pmset -g log` showed 5-second DarkWakes in the morning window and

under `/usr/bin/caffeinate -i -s` (`-s` holds only on AC; lid-shut on battery still sleeps).
**How to apply:** before tuning memsearch, line the slow window up against `pmset -g log`.
Same session: `daily-backup.ps1` now resolves `{DEV}` in index paths (it had skipped
`KeystoneOS/decisions`). Jev/TypeSafe does not help indexing: it judges, it does not embed.

### DEV/project_memsearch-index-is-destructive.md

---
name: memsearch-index-is-destructive
description: "`memsearch index <paths>` deletes every indexed source outside the given paths — never run it with a partial or test path set; plus the 2026-10-07 Windows failure causes (history: Windows no longer indexes)"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 4f57cc78-0bf6-4202-bd61-8f428a3c6dca
  modified: 2026-10-24T15:00:22.564Z
---

`memsearch index <paths>` is **never read-only**. It reconciles the collection against
the path set it is given and deletes every indexed source not under those paths
(core.py `index()` → store.py delete). An empty or partial path set wipes the rest.

On 2026-10-07 a diagnostic run against an empty temp dir deleted ~12,900 of ~31,000
vectors before it was stopped. Recovery: a full re-index over every path in
`KeystoneOS/data/memory-index-paths.json` (13 paths then), which took hours on Windows
(~3 s/chunk). The Mac runs ~0.7 s/chunk.
`memsearch stats` counts tombstones until compaction, so use `count(*)` for live rows.

**Why:** a "just timing it" run silently destroyed 40% of the index.
**How to apply:** never pass a test or partial path set to `memsearch index`. To time
indexing, use a throwaway collection or time `memsearch search`. For a catch-up run,
let the daily backup do it: `~/.claude/scripts/daily-backup.ps1` step 2c reads the full
path set from `memory-index-paths.json` and takes the hook's `.memsearch-index.lock`.
It runs once a day, so by hand use `node ~/.claude/hooks/memsearch-sync.js --worker`
(same path set and lock; it skips if an index started in the last 30 min).
Superseded 2026-10-24: this used to name `~/.claude/scripts/memsearch-drain.ps1`; the
Windows drain chain was retired and its scripts deleted (see [[automation-cadence]]).

Windows failure causes found the same day. Superseded 2026-10-24: history only. Docker
was removed from the laptop, there is no Milvus standalone, and Windows runs no indexing
(see [[work-laptop-hands-off]]). The 3h hook cap still holds on the Mac.
- **10-06 "Milvus unreachable":** Docker Desktop's vpnkit port forward to
  milvus-standalone flapped after days of uptime through Modern Standby. Milvus itself
  never restarted. A Docker restart cleared it.
- **10-07 ETIMEDOUT ×9:** low free RAM (1–2 GB) slowed indexing to ~1.2 s/chunk, so the
  hook's 600s cap killed every run partway. The cap was raised to 3h on 2026-10-07.
  The streak never resets on Windows because no nightly reindex runs there.

### DEV/project_memsearch-index-path-drift.md

---
name: memsearch-index-path-drift
description: "the SessionEnd memsearch hook read its path config from a Windows-era ~/Desktop/DEV path and silently fell back, indexing 4 of 10 memory paths for months after the Mac migration"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  modified: 2026-10-24T14:53:27.089Z
  originSessionId: 75381393-88b6-4b65-960d-6613e08f7060
---

`~/DEV/KeystoneOS/data/memory-index-paths.json` is the single source of truth for which directories memsearch indexes. Three writers read it: the SessionEnd hook `~/.claude/hooks/memsearch-sync.js`, `~/.claude/scripts/daily-backup.ps1` (nightly; 09:00 since 2026-08-29), and the Codex hook `KeystoneOS/scripts/codex-hooks/memsearch-sync.ps1`. **Current 2026-10-24:** the daily backup runs hourly 12:00-17:00 on AC power through `daily-backup-login.sh` (since 2026-10-22). The Codex `.ps1` folder is gone; Codex runs the same `.js` through the `~/.codex/hooks` symlink. `recall.py` and `remember.py` also read the JSON now.

**Found 2026-08-14:** the JS hook pointed at `~/Desktop/DEV/KeystoneOS/data/memory-index-paths.json` — the pre-migration Windows layout. DEV lives at `~/DEV` on this Mac, so the read threw, the `catch` returned a hardcoded fallback, and the hook indexed **4 paths instead of 10** for months. The fallback itself was also stale (`~/Desktop/SecondBrain/...`, which does not exist since the vault move). `daily-backup.ps1` used `$U/DEV` and was already correct; the Codex hook self-locates from its own script path and was fine. So only the JS hook drifted — and it is the one wired into `settings.json` (`SessionEnd`, 50s timeout). Since 2026-09-02 that hook hands the index to a detached worker and exits at once, so the 50s no longer bounds the index: see [[memsearch-hook-timeout-cap]].

Unindexed as a result: `SecondBrain/Knowledge`, `SecondBrain/Inbox/meetings`, `SecondBrain/morning-briefings`, the Mac memory slug `-Users-kristinarash-DEV/memory`, `KeystoneOS/decisions`, `.codex/memories`. Incremental recall for all of those depended entirely on that nightly.

**Why:** the failure mode was invisible. A silent `catch → fallback` means a migration-broken config path degrades into a quieter, smaller, still-succeeding job — no error, no log line, no failed run. Nothing surfaces until someone asks "why didn't that turn up in search?" The bug was not the wrong path; it was that the wrong path cost nothing to have.

**How to apply:**
- Any config-file fallback in this stack must log to `.errors.log` when it fires. The JS hook now does. A fallback that never announces itself is a silent outage with a long tail.
- When auditing post-migration breakage, grep for `Desktop/DEV` and `Desktop/SecondBrain` — those two strings mark Windows-era assumptions. Do not trust that a script "works" as evidence its paths resolved; check what it actually resolved to.
- Verify path config by resolving it in isolation (`node -e` reading the same JSON, printing EXISTS/MISSING per entry) rather than by running the indexer — that proves the fix without taking the Milvus Lite write lock.
- Paths in the JSON that do not exist yet are harmless; every writer filters through an existence check before passing them to memsearch.

**There were TWO copies of this hook, and fixing one did not fix the other (2026-08-15).** A Codex review found `~/.codex/hooks.json` wires its *own* copy at `~/.codex/hooks/memsearch-sync.js`, separate from the Claude copy at `~/.claude/hooks/memsearch-sync.js`. The Claude copy was repaired 2026-08-14; the Codex copy still pointed at `~/Desktop/DEV/...`, so **every Codex session-end indexed a stale 5-path fallback** that also referenced the old `~/Desktop/SecondBrain` — missing SecondBrain/Knowledge, Inbox/meetings, morning-briefings, KeystoneOS decisions and the Mac memory slug. Now fixed and verified resolving all 11 configured paths.

Ordering trap in that repair: `const ERR_LOG` was declared *after* `const PATHS = resolvePaths()`. Adding a `logErr()` call inside `resolvePaths` therefore hit the const temporal dead zone, and `logErr`'s own `try/catch` swallowed the ReferenceError — reproducing the silent fallback the fix was meant to remove. `ERR_LOG` must be declared before `PATHS`.

**How to apply:** when fixing a hook, first ask *which copy the harness actually wires* — check `~/.codex/hooks.json` and `~/.claude/settings.json`, not just the file you happened to open. Grep the whole home tree for the hook's basename before assuming there is one.

**A THIRD hook had the same stale path, found 2026-09-01 during `/doctor-plus`.** `~/.claude/hooks/keystone-unified-snapshot.js` (SessionStart) read `~/Desktop/DEV/KeystoneOS/outputs/dashboard/unified-snapshot.md`, threw ENOENT, and its `catch (_) { emit(null) }` injected **nothing at all** — for every session since the migration. The snapshot file was being written correctly the whole time at `~/DEV/KeystoneOS/outputs/dashboard/`; only the reader was wrong. Zero symptoms: no error, no log, valid JSON on stdout, session starts normally.

The 2026-08-14/15 sweep fixed the two `memsearch-sync.js` copies but did not catch this one, so **"grep for `Desktop/DEV`" must cover every file in `~/.claude/hooks/` and `~/.codex/hooks/`, not only the hook currently being repaired.** Run it as a sweep across the whole hooks tree, not per-file.

That sweep then found a **fourth** copy — `~/.codex/hooks/keystone-unified-snapshot.js`, byte-identical and wired in `~/.codex/hooks.json`. Also fixed 2026-09-01.

**Superseded 2026-10-24:** `~/.codex/hooks` is now a symlink to `~/.claude/hooks`, so every hook has one copy and the two-copies story above is history. See [[hook-two-copies-trap]]. The habit still holds for other config pairs: ask which copy the harness reads.

**A second signature the `Desktop/DEV` grep cannot catch:** `~/.codex/AGENTS.md` (dated 2026-08-08) had been through a bad `claude` to `Codex` find-replace, so it told Codex to read `~/.Codex/global-memory/`, `~/.Codex/projects/<slug>/memory/` and `~/.Codex/Codex-memory-compiler/daily/` — none of which exist. Grep for `.Codex` (capital C) as well as `Desktop/DEV` when auditing migration damage. Also check which AGENTS.md the harness actually reads: `~/.claude/AGENTS.md` was correct but referenced by nothing.

Resolved 2026-09-01: `~/.codex/AGENTS.md` is now a symlink to `~/.claude/AGENTS.md`, so the pair has one home and cannot drift again. `setup-agents-symlinks.sh` was also sourcing `CLAUDE.md` for that link — the one thing `CLAUDE.md` explicitly forbids — and now sources `AGENTS.md`. Running that script used to recreate the bug.

Repaired 2026-09-01: path corrected to `~/DEV`, required sources now push a visible "SessionStart hook could not read a required memory file" block into `additionalContext` instead of failing silently, and the hook now also injects `global-memory/USER.md` + `MEMORY.md` (replacing a prose rule in `CLAUDE.md` that nothing enforced). The KeystoneOS snapshot is pointed at, not pasted.

Related: [[milvus-lock-misdiagnosis]] (found while fixing that), [[secondbrain-vault-location]] (the vault move that stranded the fallback), [[backup-sync-system]]

### DEV/project_milvus-lock-misdiagnosis.md

---
name: milvus-lock-misdiagnosis
description: milvus-lite reports lock contention as a version-incompatibility error; following its advice destroys a working memsearch index for hours
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: fa062f93-2c55-4016-b9c6-f1a32e0a7083
  modified: 2026-08-15T02:42:26.304Z
---

When memsearch fails to open `~/.memsearch/milvus.db`, milvus-lite prints:

> Failed to open the local Milvus Lite database. If this database was created with an older Milvus Lite release, it may not be compatible with Milvus Lite 3.x. Move the existing .db file aside, then rebuild the index...

**That text is a generic open-failure string, not a version verdict.** It fires just as readily on plain lock contention. Diagnosed 2026-08-14: the underlying error was `BlockingIOError: [Errno 35]` from `flock`, and `lsof +D ~/.memsearch/milvus.db` named the holder — a concurrent manual `memsearch index` running after the SecondBrain vault move. The same DB with the same milvus-lite 3.1.1 had indexed successfully hours earlier.

(Attribution caution: at the time this was written the holder was assumed to be "another Claude session," inferred from an unfamiliar PID and shell-snapshot id. Eric corrected that — it was not. `lsof` tells you *which process*, never *which agent or person*; state the process and leave the actor unnamed.)

**Why:** following the message's advice (move the .db aside, rebuild) throws away a working index and costs an hours-scale re-index of the SecondBrain library — a self-inflicted outage in response to a transient collision.

**How to apply:**
- Before believing any milvus-lite "incompatible database" message, run `lsof +D ~/.memsearch/milvus.db` and `ps aux | grep memsearch`. A live holder means wait, not rebuild.
- Milvus Lite is single-writer. `daily-backup.ps1`'s advisory lock (`.memsearch-index.lock`, ~line 416) coordinates the nightly reindex with the SessionEnd hook only — it cannot see a hand-run `memsearch index`, so manual indexing during a backup window collides. Avoid running `memsearch index` by hand while the nightly backup may fire.
- `memsearch-index:full-set` in `.errors.log` is therefore usually transient. Confirm the lock is free, then let the next scheduled run clear it.

**Tooling mitigation added 2026-08-14 (because the written warning was not enough).** Later the same day a session ran `memsearch reset --yes` anyway and triggered a ~2h full rebuild — the exact outage this note warns about, with the note already on disk. Prose guidance does not survive contact with a scary error message, so the guard is now in code:

- `~/.local/bin/ms-search` — lock-aware retry wrapper for reads (`search` / `stats` / `expand` / `transcript`; write subcommands are refused). Retries with backoff to 60s (`MS_SEARCH_MAX_WAIT`), then exits **75** saying the DB is healthy and not to run `reset`. It retries **only** on `DataDirLockedError` / `another process holds the lock` / `Resource temporarily unavailable` / `_acquire_lock` / `fcntl.flock`; it deliberately does **not** key on the "may not be compatible with Milvus Lite 3.x" sentence, since that same wording is emitted for genuine incompatibility — so real corruption still fails fast and passes its exit code through.
- `~/.claude/hooks/memsearch-sync.js` now classifies those same lock signatures as transient instead of escalating them as hard errors. Caveat: `bumpTransientStreak` shares one counter across all transient classes at threshold 6, so a cluster of session-ends during a long rebuild can still escalate — downgraded, not eliminated.

**How to apply (updated):** prefer `ms-search "query"` over `memsearch search` for recall; it waits out a busy index instead of surfacing the misleading message. Reserve bare `memsearch` for writes.

Related: [[backup-sync-system]] (carries the earlier two-writer lesson), [[memsearch-index-path-drift]] (the config drift found while fixing this), [[drive-fuse-rsync-mtime-loop]]

### DEV/project_path-shadowing-and-cleanup.md

---
name: path-shadowing-and-cleanup
description: "PATH shadowing repair 2026-08-13 — measure PATH with env -i, grep hardcoded paths before deleting a binary, broken symlinks evade find -type f"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  modified: 2026-10-23T16:07:47.830Z

---

Repairs made 2026-08-13 on this Mac, and the four traps hit doing it. All four generalise.

**What was wrong and is now fixed:**
- `uv` existed twice — `~/.local/bin/uv` 0.11.6 (Apr) shadowed Homebrew's 0.12.1 (Jul), so a
  three-month-old build was winning. Fixed with `uv self update` → 0.12.3, then `brew uninstall uv`.
- PATH had duplicate `~/go/bin` and `~/.local/bin` entries (17 entries → 15). Sources: a redundant
  export in `.zshrc`, a duplicated `go/bin` line, and two unguarded `brew shellenv` calls in `.zprofile`.
- An entire pre-migration Node install at `/usr/local` (~690 MB: node, npm, npx, corepack, stale
  codex/gemini/gws) removed. `/usr/local/bin` now holds only Docker Desktop + kubectl.
- `FIREFLIES_API_KEY` moved from plaintext in `.zshrc` into the login Keychain.

**The four traps — these are the reusable part:**

1. **A PATH read from inside a tool shell is a lie.** Any earlier `export PATH=…` in the session
   pollutes it. This produced a wrong claim (`~/.bun/bin` reported as duplicated when it was not).
   Honest measurement:
   `env -i HOME="$HOME" USER="$USER" TERM=xterm SHELL=/bin/zsh /bin/zsh -lic 'echo $PATH'`
2. **PATH order only governs lookups by name.** Deleting `~/.local/bin/uv` would have silently
   killed three hooks in `~/.claude/settings.json` (SessionStart/PreCompact/SessionEnd) that call
   the memory-compiler by *absolute path*. Always `grep -rl '/full/path' ~/.claude ~/DEV` first.
3. **Scheduled jobs are the blind spot.** Eight KeystoneOS launchd agents referenced `/usr/local`
   — harmlessly, as PATH entries — but nothing in shell config would have shown them. Check
   `~/Library/LaunchAgents` before touching a shared prefix.
4. **`[ -e ]` and `find -type f` both skip broken symlinks.** 92 npm man pages were symlinks into
   a just-deleted tree; the first cleanup pass removed 1 of 92 and reported success. Use
   `find … \( -type l -o -type f \) -delete`.

**Done 2026-10-22:** Eric rotated the Fireflies key; the old value left in transcripts and
`file-history/` is dead. The two `.zshrc.bak-20260813-*` backups went to `~/.Trash` on 2026-10-23.

**Still open (his action):** `sudo rm -rf /usr/local/include/node` (62 MB) and `sudo rmdir /usr/local/lib/node_modules`.

**Why:** each of these cost real debugging time, and three of them fail *silently* — the wrong
version runs, the hook stops, the file never gets deleted, with no error.
**How to apply:** before asserting where a tool lives or deleting any binary on this machine, run
the `env -i` measurement and the hardcoded-path grep. See also [[zsh-shell-traps]] and
[[terminal-fluency-workspace]].

### DEV/project_printing-press-spec-traps.md

---
name: printing-press-spec-traps
description: "Spec-authoring and pipeline traps discovered printing catapult + zotero CLIs (Aug 2026) — pagination params, envelope-nested fields, probe fixtures"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: a86cfb00-e6d1-46b9-8cdc-35e21acd9931
  modified: 2026-08-06T23:21:52.213Z
---

Traps hit while printing `catapult-openfield-connect` and `zotero-research-library` (2026-08-05/06), each cost a debugging cycle:

- **Offset pagination MUST name `cursor_param`** in the spec (e.g. `cursor_param: start` for Zotero). Omitted, the generator defaults to `after`; servers that ignore unknown params return page 1 forever while the cursor climbs (silent infinite loop, same 25 rows).
- **Envelope-nested APIs leave all extracted store columns empty.** Zotero items nest fields under `$.data.*`; the store's `LookupFieldValue` reads top-level keys only, so title/date_added/name columns are NULL. Hand commands must read `json_extract("data", '$.data.<field>')` and search via `resources_fts` (joins on its `id` column — NEVER on rowid, which is hashed).
- **Novel command names collide with framework commands** (`search`, `periods`) — validate-narrative catches it late; check the framework command list at absorb time. Renamed to `ground`.
- **Dogfood probes run with PP_DOGFOOD=1** which curtails syncs to one page — happy-args fixtures must resolve against a ~25-row cache. Use dynamic specials (`top`, `last`) instead of baked keys.
- **`pp:happy-args` grammar**: positional labels need angle brackets (`<query>=hamstring`); `--flag=value` tokens pass flags; probes time out at 30s so unbounded commands need a bounding flag in happy-args.
- **generate --force preserves hand files but re-emits generated docs** — keep a `fix-generated-docs.py` per run to strip phantom "Covered paths" bullets after every regen.
- **Novel child commands must use direct `cmd.AddCommand(newXxxCmd(...))` calls.** The public library's SKILL.md verifier discovers subcommands by regex-scanning for that exact pattern; any helper indirection (e.g. `addNovelCommandIfAbsent`) hides children and their flags, failing CI on doc examples. Guard with a `hasSubcommandNamed` check instead of wrapping AddCommand.
- **Zotero /deleted returns a category map** (collections/items/searches/tags/settings arrays in one object), not a list — generic extractors keep only `items` and silently drop the rest; flatten all categories into keyed tombstones.
- **Catapult API v6**: date filter on POST /stats hangs server-side — express windows as activity_id sets; `requested_only=false` needed for athlete/activity/date columns; dates arrive MM/DD/YYYY.
- Related: [[zsh-shell-traps]]

---
name: s2-cognition-analysis
description: "S2 Cognition data traps (vendor reference group, P/K short battery, invalid reports) and the standing rule that any flagging threshold must be null-calibrated and pre-registered before the data is touched"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 856bd54e-8db3-42f5-a770-103ee081614e
  modified: 2026-08-16T18:37:34.242Z
---

S2 Cognition analysis lives at `~/DEV/S2_Evaluation` (private repo `erash11/S2_Evaluation`). V1 shipped 2026-08-16 with a **null finding**: no offensive lineman is cognitively atypical once the flagging threshold is calibrated against a null model.

**Vendor data traps** (learned the hard way, not documented by S2):

- Percentiles are scored against **"NFL PROSPECTS - ALL POSITIONS"**, not a college or position-specific reference group. So a percentile is only comparable *within* that reference group — cross-position pooling is legitimate (Baylor rooms range 42nd–82nd), but "50th percentile" does not mean "average for his position."
- The **P/K battery has only 7 measures**, not the usual 9, with zero N/A cells. That is structural to the vendor's short battery, not a parse bug — don't chase it.
- Some reports fail S2's own **validity check**; the vendor marks them INVALID. Exclude them from analysis and surface as a retest recommendation instead of silently dropping.
- Test years are mixed across a roster. Flag the year as a diagnostic; don't filter on it.

**Standing methodological rule** (ADR 0013, applies beyond S2): never set a "flag the outlier" threshold without first simulating what a **pure-noise room** produces at that threshold. The original 1.5 SD rule flagged 10 of 15 linemen; a homogeneous null room flags 7–13 of 15, so the rule was measuring nothing. Related: with 9 categories, max-over-N inflation makes almost any naive threshold vacuous.

Corollary — because Eric is his own reviewer on side-lane projects, thresholds get **pre-registered in a timestamped git commit before the data is on the machine**. Changing a threshold after seeing results requires a new ADR stating what was wrong; never retune silently.

### DEV/project_settings-json-bom-trap.md

---
name: settings-json-bom-trap
description: "A bad Windows write to ~/.claude config files does TWO things at once — adds a UTF-8 BOM (dcg then reports the hook as missing) and CP1252-double-encodes every non-ASCII character (statusline bars turn to junk). Check settings.json, CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md, and check for both faults."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 7741462f-dac7-4551-8692-76574bbfd202
  modified: 2026-10-24T14:51:28.734Z
---

One bad write from the Windows machine damages `~/.claude` config files in
**two independent ways**. They arrive together and are fixed together, but they
surface at completely different times, so finding one does not mean you found
both. On 2026-09-10 only the BOM was caught; the mojibake sat undetected for two
more days until the statusline was looked at directly on 2026-09-11.

## Fault 1 — the UTF-8 BOM (loud, misleading)

`~/.claude/settings.json` acquires a **UTF-8 BOM** — the 3 invisible bytes
`EF BB BF` at the start. Claude Code parses the file anyway, so nothing in
Claude Code looks broken. `dcg` (Destructive Command Guard) does not, so it
prints at every session start:

```
[dcg] Hook missing from ~/.claude/settings.json — run: dcg install
```

**The message is wrong, and its suggested fix is the wrong fix.** The hook was
present and correct all along. Running `dcg install` would have added a second
hook to a file the tool cannot read.

**Diagnose, don't trust the banner.** `dcg doctor` names the real fault:

```
Checking hook wiring... ERROR
  Invalid JSON: expected value at line 1 column 1
```

"Line 1 column 1" on a file that is visibly valid JSON means a BOM.

## Fault 2 — CP1252 double-encoding (silent, cosmetic-looking)

The same write reads the file's UTF-8 bytes as **CP1252**, then saves them back
as UTF-8. Every non-ASCII character becomes 2–3 junk characters. Nothing errors.
Nothing warns. JSON stays valid. You only notice by *looking at rendered output*.

The statusline is where it shows, because it is the only config that draws
box characters:

| Intended | Becomes | Where |
|---|---|---|
| `░` U+2591 | `â–‘` | statusline meter bar (empty) |
| `▓` U+2593 | `â–“` | statusline meter bar (filled) |
| `↑ ↓ →` | `â†‘ â†“ â†’` | git ahead/behind, cache arrow |
| `—` em-dash | `â€”` | CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md prose |
| `…` `’` `·` | `â€¦` `â€™` `Â·` | CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md prose |

The `â` prefix is the tell — it is `0xE2`, the first byte of most UTF-8 symbols,
read as Latin-1.

## It is not only settings.json

The 2026-09-11 sweep found the damage in **three** files. Two of them also
carried BOMs that the 9/10 fix never looked at:

- `~/.claude/settings.json` — 113 mangled chars (no BOM by then, already fixed)
- `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` — 8 mangled chars **+ BOM**
- `~/.claude/AGENTS.md` — 25 mangled chars **+ BOM**

Always sweep the whole tree, never just the file that complained.

## Fix — strip BOM, then reverse the encoding, then verify rendering

```python
import json
p = "/Users/kristinarash/.claude/settings.json"
s = open(p, encoding="utf-8").read().lstrip("﻿")
fixed = s.encode("cp1252").decode("utf-8")   # exact inverse
json.loads(fixed)                             # must still parse
open(p, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="\n").write(fixed)
```

`.encode("cp1252")` raising means the file is only *partly* mangled, or a BOM is
still present — strip the BOM first, and never force the round-trip on a file
where it fails. Sweep for survivors by scanning for these patterns:

```python
pats = ['â–‘','â–“','â†‘','â†“','â†’','â€”','â€™','â€¦','Â·']
```

**Verify the statusline by rendering it**, not by reading the JSON — pipe a
sample payload into the `statusLine.command` and look at the bars.

Writing the repaired file needs the Write tool, not a shell heredoc: `dcg`
blocks any truncating `>` redirect into `~` (`core.filesystem:redirect-truncate-root-home`).
**Superseded 2026-10-24:** that rule was allowlisted on 2026-10-11, so a `>` into `~` now
passes (see [[dcg-guard-blocks]]). The Python fix above writes the file itself either way.

## The generalisation

Two tolerant readers hid this for two days. Claude Code tolerates the BOM, so
the statusline kept running; the terminal tolerates mojibake, so it kept drawing
*something*. **The strict reader complains about the wrong thing (`dcg`), and the
cosmetic damage never complains at all.** When a config file has been touched by
the other machine, check the first bytes *and* grep for `â` — one fault does not
imply the other has been handled.

Related: [[dcg-guard-blocks]], [[hook-two-copies-trap]], [[github-consolidation]],
[[path-shadowing-and-cleanup]]

Measured 2026-09-12 from a gap analysis of a Nate Herk / **Mark Kashef** video
("How to Actually Choose the Right AI Agent", 2026-09-11). Full note:
`~/SecondBrain/Inbox/2026-09-12-harness-over-model-mark-kashef.md`.
Same shape as the earlier audit in [[brain-audit-loop]] — that one scored the
**vault**, this one scores the **skill layer**.

## The measurement

| Metric | Count |
|---|---|
| Global skills in `~/.claude/skills/` | 160 (→ **117** after the Tier 1 archive, 2026-09-12) |
| Plugin skills exposed per session | ~37 (6 enabled, 18 disabled) |
| SKILL.md files in plugin cache | 606 — disabled plugins + old versions, NOT the load |
| Project-level skills anywhere in `~/DEV` | **0** |
| `.jsonl` sessions scanned | 414 |
| Distinct real skills **ever** invoked | **58** |
| Used 3+ times | 30 |
| Used exactly once | 19 |

Everything is global. That is the anti-pattern, not the achievement.

## The rule that fixes it — promotion

**Everything stays project-level until it earns global.** A skill lives in
`<project>/.claude/skills/` until it proves itself across 2+ projects, then it
gets promoted to `~/.claude/skills/`. Keeps the global load small and the blast
radius tight — so when something underperforms you can tell a *model* problem
from a *harness* problem from an *organisation* problem.

## The audit question

Not "how often did I run this skill?" but **"would the model do this fine without
the skill now?"** A skill is a crutch; as the brain gets smarter the crutch starts
to *limit* it. Seasonal skills (`forecast-capture`) and occasional ones
(`ingest-book`) are low-count by design — low usage alone is not a delete signal.

## Re-measure (BUILTIN filter is the whole trick)

Without the `BUILTIN` set you also count `/exit`, `/clear`, `/compact` and friends,
which inflates the total to 74 and buries the real skills.

```bash
python3 - <<'EOF'
import glob,re,collections
BUILTIN={'exit','clear','compact','rename','color','login','logout','plugin','doctor',
'help','model','config','resume','cost','status','init','agents','mcp','hooks','memory',
'review','vim','terminal-setup','install-github-app','add-dir','bug','release-notes',
'pr-comments','ide','permissions','statusline','output-style','todos','export',
'privacy-settings','upgrade','fast','artifacts','tasks','loop','context','usage','rewind',
'sandbox','feedback','worktrees','skills','reload-skills','reload-plugins','bashes',
'keybindings','theme'}
c=collections.Counter()
for f in glob.glob('/Users/kristinarash/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl',recursive=True):
    try:
        for line in open(f,encoding='utf-8',errors='ignore'):
            if 'Skill' not in line and 'command-name' not in line: continue
            for m in re.finditer(r'"name"\s*:\s*"Skill"\s*,\s*"input"\s*:\s*\{[^}]*?"skill"\s*:\s*"([^"]+)"', line):
                c[m.group(1)]+=1
            for m in re.finditer(r'<command-name>/([a-zA-Z0-9:_-]+)</command-name>', line):
                c[m.group(1)]+=1
    except Exception: pass
real={k:v for k,v in c.items() if k.split(':')[-1] not in BUILTIN and k not in BUILTIN}
print("distinct real skills ever invoked:",len(real))
print("used >=3 times:",len([k for k,v in real.items() if v>=3]))
print("used exactly once:",len([k for k,v in real.items() if v==1]))
for k,v in sorted(real.items(),key=lambda x:-x[1]): print(f"{v:5d}  {k}")
EOF
```

## Decision, 2026-09-12

**Do the skill audit BEFORE adopting Pi** (`pi.dev`) as an alternative harness.
Rationale: the leverage is the bloat, not the harness. Auditing first means any
future harness move ports ~30 good skills instead of ~200 mixed ones.

Pi facts, verified from `pi.dev/docs/latest` 2026-09-12 — full note at
`~/SecondBrain/Inbox/2026-09-12-pi-harness-research.md`:

1. **No sandbox, no approval flows.** "Pi does not include a built-in sandbox."
   Project trust only guards resource *loading*, not what the agent then does.
   Never run Pi in `~/DEV` or near `DexaProject`. Trial it in `~/pi-trial` or a
   container (`sbx` keeps the credential off the container).
2. **Skills port for one line.** Pi implements the Agent Skills standard and already
   auto-discovers `~/.agents/skills/` — where 45 of the skills live. Add the rest with
   `{"skills": ["~/.claude/skills"]}` in `~/.pi/agent/settings.json`. It loads
   `AGENTS.md` **or** `CLAUDE.md` directly.
3. **Hooks → TypeScript extensions is a bounded port, not a rewrite** (earlier note
   said "weeks", that was wrong). Hooks here are already `.ts`; Pi's `tool_call` event
   returns `{block, reason}` — the same shape as the dcg guard.
4. **Claude subscription through Pi bills per token as "extra usage", NOT against plan
   limits.** Changes the economics of brain-swapping.

Config lives in `~/.pi/agent/` and survives npm uninstall.
See also [[hook-two-copies-trap]] and [[dcg-guard-blocks]].

## Audit outcome, 2026-09-12

**Both tiers executed.** 99 skills archived, global **160 → 61**, roster cost
**19,158 → 6,428 tokens/session (a 66% cut)**. Zero regressions: none of the 99
had ever been invoked in 414 sessions.

Decision 2026-09-12: keep the `mattpocock-skills` and `superpowers` **plugins** and
archive the local bare-name duplicates. The plugin (v1.2.3, 35 skills) ships every
duplicate removed and is newer than the July symlinks. Rule that follows: when a
plugin and a local skill share a name, **the plugin wins** — delete the local copy.

Script: the one-off `skills-audit-2026-09-12.sh` went to `~/.Trash/` on 2026-10-24 (it archived,
never deleted). Undo still works: `mv ~/.claude/skills-archive/2026-09-12/* ~/.claude/skills/`.
Report: `~/SecondBrain/Inbox/2026-09-12-skill-audit.md`.

Traps found while doing it:
1. **CORRECTED 2026-09-12 — `~/.claude/skills/` IS version-controlled.** It is its own
   git repo, remote `https://github.com/erash11/claude-skills.git`, and the audit was
   committed as `3ab4467 chore: apply global skill audit` and pushed. The earlier note
   that it is "gitignored, archive is the only undo" was true only of the *`dotclaude`*
   repo, which ignores this path — a different thing. **Git IS the safety net here, and
   it is also how the cut reaches Windows.** Undo with
   `git -C ~/.claude/skills revert <sha> && git push`, not the archive folder
   (`skills-archive/` is not in the repo and never reaches the other machine).
2. **A cut in `~/.claude/skills/` does NOT reach `~/.agents/skills/`.** After the audit,
   98 of the 99 archived skills were still live in the pool (306 entries there vs 61
   canonical). Claude Code stopped seeing them; **Pi auto-discovers that folder**, so
   installing Pi would have re-exposed all of them. Always cut both.
3. **Skills live in three places and it is easy to edit the wrong copy.**
   `~/.claude/skills/` (19 entries were symlinks pointing *out* to the pool),
   `~/.agents/skills/` (Pi, Cowork), `~/.codex/skills/` (Codex, 27 symlinks + 5 real
   dirs). Count with `find -L`; plain `find` undercounts.
4. **`sync-to-codex.sh` did `rm -rf "$dst/$s"; cp -R "$SRC/$s"`** over a 7-name
   allowlist. If `$SRC/$s` ever became a symlink into `$dst`, that deletes the real
   data. `dev-sync` tells you to run it after every pull. A `.ps1` twin has the same
   shape — patch both.
5. **`~/.claude/skills/_shared/`** holds `config.json` + `Inference/` and is resolved by
   10+ skills via `parents[2]/_shared/config.json`. It has **no SKILL.md**. Never treat
   "no SKILL.md" as "orphan, delete".
6. **"606 plugin skills" is cache, not load.** Only 6 of 24 plugins are enabled
   (~37 skills exposed). The rest are disabled plugins and old cached versions.

## Executed 2026-09-12 — traps the live run found

- **Views are live links now.** `~/.agents/skills/<owned>` and `~/.codex/skills/<owned>`
  point into canonical, so anything that writes a view path writes canonical
  (`graphify install --platform agents` does; see [[graphify-runtime-setup]]).
- **`skillOverrides` in `~/.claude/settings.json` breaks parity silently.** Codex and Pi
  ignore that file, so an owned skill set `"off"` there is hidden in Claude Code but live
  elsewhere. Perfect frontmatter does not help; `skill-portability-check.py` fails it.
  Resolved 2026-09-13: Eric re-enabled the 7 (ArXiv, ISA, Science, capture-insight,
  library-review, pp-espn, session-miner) — `~/.claude` commit `21c686d`, checker 42/42.
  Never set an owned skill "off" again; retire it from canonical instead.
- **Git's spelling wins, not the Mac's.** APFS is case-insensitive: the folder showed
  `Harvest` while git recorded `harvest/`. Check `git ls-files` before "fixing" a
  name to match the disk.
- **A `closeout` in another session commits your uncommitted work** (it swept Task 5's
  34 SKILL.md edits into its own commit). Commit each verified step immediately.
- **Description budget:** keep each description under ~650 chars; Claude Code caps the
  combined listing.

## Architecture decided 2026-09-12 (executed through Task 5 the same day)

**Canonical = `~/.claude/skills/`** (the git repo, real directories only, **never commit
a symlink** — Windows pulls this repo). `~/.agents/skills/` and `~/.codex/skills/` are
**generated views**, rebuilt by `sync-to-codex.sh` from a complete manifest of every
canonical dir holding a SKILL.md, recorded in a `.generated-by-sync-to-codex` ownership
file so an audit can tell a generated entry from a third-party `npx skills add` install.
Symlink on Mac, copy on Windows.

Portable frontmatter contract (fires in Claude Code *and* Codex): `name` must equal the
directory name (TitleCase is legal), and `description` needs **both** a positive
"Use when …" clause with literal trigger phrases *and* a negative "Do not use …" clause.
Codex reads only `name` + `description` (+ optional `metadata.short-description`) and
ignores `argument-hint` / `allowed-tools`. Codex over-fires without the negative clause;
Claude will not trigger without the literal phrases.

Plan (Codex-approved after 6 review rounds, 10→0 findings):
`~/DEV/KeystoneOS/docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-12-harness-agnostic-aios.md`.
See [[dev-layout-and-discovery]], [[hook-two-copies-trap]], [[vendored-skill-install]].

## claude.ai-synced duplicates, 2026-10-02 (doctor-plus)

`~/.claude/skills/synced/<account-id>/` is claude.ai account skills synced down (gitignored,
re-synced each start — deleting the folder does not stick). They list as `anthropic-skills:<name>`.
Where one duplicates a local skill, **local wins**: set `"anthropic-skills:<name>": "off"` in
`skillOverrides` (namespaced keys work — verified with a headless on/off control run). Done for

in canonical 2026-10-02 after a 9/10 removal left untracked per-machine copies). Do not delete them on claude.ai: the synced
five-slides is written for the claude.ai sandbox and is the right copy there. The "never off" rule
above is for *owned* skills only.

## Listing trim, 2026-09-14 (doctor-plus)

**40 owned skills are `"name-only"` in `~/.claude/settings.json` `skillOverrides`**
(dotclaude commit `172d547`). 13 stay full: the ones Claude invoked itself 2+ times

**Mission:** fluency at the command line specifically to drive Claude Code and Codex rather than
the desktop/web UIs — control, composability, headless runs. *Not* general shell mastery; writing
shell scripts and building CLIs are out of scope (the latter is [[printing-press-spec-traps]]).

**To resume:** `cd ~/DEV/Terminal_Fluency`, then read `MISSION.md` → `NOTES.md` (teaching
preferences, verified environment, lesson ledger) → newest `learning-records/`. Self-describing by
design; do **not** re-interview about the mission. Lessons 01–03 done; 04 is sessions/permission

**How he learns — the single most useful fact here.** Twice now the pattern has been: learn a
concept → find it applies to a real defect on his own machine → fix it → ask for the next lesson.
Build drills from his actual files and tools, never synthetic examples. A lesson that ends in a
real repair sticks; an exercise does not.

**Non-obvious traps, all learned the hard way:**

---
name: third-party-skill-install
description: "After installing a vendored third-party skill: the pre-commit/daily-backup jam that sync-to-codex.sh clears, why the install never reaches the other machine, and the CreateSkill warning; layout and steps are in vendored-skill-install"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 0804822d-4ddb-4933-801e-9a07f13445ae
  modified: 2026-10-24T14:54:46.918Z
---

Layout and install steps (real files in `~/.agents/skills/<name>`, symlinked out; checked
on the Mac): see [[vendored-skill-install]]. This file covers what happens after.

One clone means one `git pull` updates every harness. Claude Code registers a new skill
**live, mid-session** — no restart needed.

**Windows trap — `ln -s` silently copies** (historical: the laptop has had no terminal work
since 2026-10-14, see [[work-laptop-hands-off]]). Git Bash's default `ln -s` duplicates the
directory instead of linking. Claude Code still finds the skill, so it *looks* installed,
but the copy has no `.git` and `git pull` silently stops being the update path. Use
`MSYS=winsymlinks:nativestrict ln -s <target> <link>`, and verify from PowerShell —
`(Get-Item <path> -Force).LinkType` must print `SymbolicLink`. `ls -la` in Git Bash shows
`l... ->` for both cases, so it is **not** sufficient proof on its own. Same MSYS family as
[[git-bash-msys-ad-stall]], different mechanism.

**The daily-backup jam.** `~/.claude/skills` is its own repo with a `pre-commit` hook
that refuses any symlink (git mode 120000), while `daily-backup.ps1` runs `git add -A` on
it. So a freshly added third-party symlink sits as `?? <name>` and will **jam the daily
backup commit** until the exclude block is regenerated.

**The fix is `bash ~/.claude/skills/sync-to-codex.sh` on the Mac, not a hand edit**
(`sync-to-codex.ps1` is the Windows twin). It classifies every
symlink in `~/.claude/skills` as THIRD_PARTY, drops it from the git index ("removed
third-party link '<name>' from the index (left on disk)"), and rewrites the generated block
in `.git/info/exclude` — which is marked *"Rewritten on every sync. Per-machine. Do not
edit by hand."* Supports `DRY_RUN=1`; dry-run first and confirm zero `retire`/`REFUSE`/
`FATAL` lines before applying.

**Why the sync cannot clobber the clone:** its copy loop touches only `$MANAGED` entries
(real directories in canonical with a SKILL.md), and its retirement loop only removes names
present in the *previous* manifest. A third-party name enters neither list, so
`~/.agents/skills/<name>` and its `.git` survive every sync. Verified — sync ran clean over
41 managed + 7 third-party with the clone intact on `main`.

**Do not route these through `CreateSkill`.** Canonicalizing an upstream repo (TitleCase,
`Workflows/`) rewrites files git tracks and breaks `git pull`. The `skills/CLAUDE.md`
mandate governs skills Eric *owns*, not vendored ones.

**A third-party install never reaches the other machine.** Corrected 2026-10-24: the
reason is not the dotclaude gitignore. `~/.claude/skills/` is its own git repo
(`erash11/claude-skills`), and owned skills do travel through it
([[skill-bloat-and-promotion]]). But the sync above keeps third-party links out of that
repo on purpose, and `~/.agents` is not a repo at all. So each machine needs its own install.

Established 2026-09-18 on Windows, installing `grill-with-ui` (not installed on the Mac). Related:
[[dev-layout-and-discovery]], [[keystoneos-verification-habits]]

### DEV/project_vendored-skill-install.md

---
name: vendored-skill-install
description: "Installing a third-party skill so Claude Code, Codex and Cowork can all use it — the canonical store, the two symlinks, the CLI flag trap, and why Cowork is different"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: a6dfb3da-c339-44b1-a836-2a6884e07ea6
  modified: 2026-10-24T14:53:01.947Z
---

Third-party skills live in **`~/.agents/skills/<name>/`** (the real files) with
`~/.agents/.skill-lock.json` as the install ledger. Both harness
directories are symlinks into it:

- `~/.claude/skills/<name>` → `../../.agents/skills/<name>` (relative)
- `~/.codex/skills/<name>` → `~/.claude/skills/<name>` (absolute, hopping through
  the Claude symlink — verified on disk 2026-09-04, and again 2026-10-24 for
  `pp-espn`, `pp-fireflies`, `anti-sleep`). One link (`scroll-craft`) points straight at
  `~/.agents/skills/` instead; both shapes resolve.
- On the Mac there is no `~/.cursor/skills`, and `~/.gemini/skills` holds real folders,
  not links (checked 2026-10-24).

Install with the CLI that owns that store when you can:

```bash
npx -y skills@latest add <owner>/<repo> -g -a claude-code -a codex -s <skill> -y
```

**Trap: in Claude Code auto mode the CLI itself is blocked.** The permission
classifier denies `npx -y skills@latest add …` outright (hit 2026-09-04).
Hand-install is then the working route, and it is enough — the files plus the two
symlinks are all a harness needs:

```bash
mkdir -p ~/.agents/skills/NAME
cp REPO/CAT/NAME/SKILL.md ~/.agents/skills/NAME/
cp -R REPO/CAT/NAME/scripts REPO/CAT/NAME/agents ~/.agents/skills/NAME/   # when present
chmod +x ~/.agents/skills/NAME/scripts/*.sh
ln -s ../../.agents/skills/NAME ~/.claude/skills/NAME
ln -s ~/.claude/skills/NAME ~/.codex/skills/NAME
```

Copy `agents/openai.yaml` too whenever the skill ships one — it is the
Codex-facing manifest, and dropping it leaves Codex with a half install.

**Trap: never put `rm -rf` in the install script.** The `dcg` PreToolUse guard
blocks the *entire* command on rule `core.filesystem:rm-rf-general`, even when the
target is a subfolder you just created yourself. Copy only what you want instead of
copy-then-delete. `dcg` also false-positives on a `>` inside a heredoc'd Python
script (rule `core.filesystem:redirect-truncate-root-home`) — use the Edit tool for
that write rather than fighting the pattern. **Superseded 2026-10-24:** that rule and
`heredoc.posix:pipeline-consumer` were allowlisted on 2026-10-11, so a `>` in a heredoc
now passes. The `rm -rf` block above is still a kept hard stop. See [[dcg-guard-blocks]].

**Trap: a hand-install is invisible to the ledger.** It gets no entry in
`~/.agents/.skill-lock.json`, so `skills update` will never touch it.
`skillFolderHash` is not a plain sha1 of the files and is not worth
reverse-engineering — have Eric run the official `add` command himself behind a `!`
prefix to register it.

**Trap: `-a` will not take a comma-separated list.** `-a claude-code,codex`
fails with "Invalid agents: claude-code,codex" and then prints a valid-agent
list containing both names. Repeat the flag instead.

**Trap: the installer does not always wire Codex.** It reports
`universal: Codex` and creates no symlink. Check
`ls -l ~/.codex/skills/<name>` after every install and make the symlink by hand
if it is missing.

The CLI runs a security scan and may report alerts. Read
`https://skills.sh/<owner>/<repo>` before trusting a skill.

**Cowork cannot take a locally-dropped skill.** Its store is
`~/Library/Application Support/Claude/local-agent-mode-sessions/skills-plugin/<a>/<b>/skills/`
with a sibling `manifest.json`, and every entry carries a **server-minted id**
(`skill_01…`). A folder placed there is not in the manifest and is wiped on the
next sync. The only route is a zip uploaded through claude.ai → Settings →
Capabilities → Skills, with the skill folder at the zip root. Expect Cowork's
sandbox to lack ffmpeg/Chrome, so any skill's verification or media step will
not run there even after a successful upload.

Where a skill puts its *output* is separate: some resolve a workspace from the
nearest `.git` walking up, so run them from inside the target project or set
their env override, or builds land wherever cwd happened to be.

See [[vendored-skill-repair]] for what to do when one of these is broken,
[[third-party-skill-install]] for the daily-backup jam a new link causes, and
[[path-shadowing-and-cleanup]] before deleting any copy.

### DEV/project_vendored-skill-repair.md

---
name: vendored-skill-repair
description: "A vendored skill fails silently or with a confusing error — check for removed ffmpeg flags first, patch every live copy, and expect the fix to revert on update"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: a6dfb3da-c339-44b1-a836-2a6884e07ea6
  modified: 2026-09-02T23:05:23.955Z
---

When a third-party skill produces **empty output rather than an error**, suspect
a CLI flag the underlying tool has since removed, not the skill's own logic.

**The instance (2026-09-02):** `/watch` returned zero frames with no useful
message. Cause: `frames.py` passed ffmpeg `-vsync`, removed in ffmpeg 7+. This
machine runs **ffmpeg 9.0.1**. Fix is `-vsync` → `-fps_mode` (same `vfr` value,
same position, exists since ffmpeg 5.0).

**Patch every live copy, and know which ones matter.** A skill can exist three
times on this machine:

1. `~/.agents/skills/<name>/…` — the vendor store, serves `~/.claude/skills/` and Codex.
2. `~/.claude/plugins/cache/<plugin>/<skill>/<version>/skills/<name>/…` — the
   plugin copy. **This is the one a `/slash` invocation actually loads.** Patch
   only the vendor store and the skill stays broken.
3. The Cowork copy under `Library/Application Support/Claude/…` — **do not
   patch.** It is server-synced and reverts. See [[vendored-skill-install]].

Confirm which file is live by reading the "Base directory for this skill" line
the harness prints when the skill loads.

**Every such patch is temporary.** Check upstream before assuming a fix is
needed, and after patching, assume `skills update` or a plugin update reinstalls
the bug. For `/watch` the upstream is `bradautomates/claude-video`, still
carrying `-vsync` as of its 2026-06-30 commit.

Verify by running the affected code path and **counting the output**, not by
reading the exit code — the original failure exited 0.

### DEV/project_zsh-shell-traps.md

---
name: zsh-shell-traps
description: "zsh-specific shell traps hit repeatedly on this macOS machine — path/UID/status reserved variables, word-splitting"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: a86cfb00-e6d1-46b9-8cdc-35e21acd9931
  modified: 2026-08-07T00:53:25.947Z
---

zsh quirks that have repeatedly broken scripts in Claude sessions on this machine:

- **Never use `path` as a variable name** — zsh ties lowercase `path` (array) to `PATH`; assigning it a scalar clobbers PATH mid-script ("command not found" for everything after).
- `UID` and `status` are read-only in zsh — use `ZUID`, `st`, etc.
- Unquoted `$VAR` does NOT word-split in zsh — use `${=VAR}` when splitting is intended.
- Background-task shells get a minimal PATH; start scripts with `export PATH="/usr/bin:/bin:/opt/homebrew/bin:$PATH"` and use `$HOME/go/bin` for Go CLIs.
- `head` at the end of a pipeline masks grep's exit code — use `grep -q` for presence tests, never `grep -l ... | head && echo FOUND`.
- **git fetch/push/pull to private repos hangs silently** in sandboxed/background shells — no keychain access means git blocks on an invisible credential prompt (looks exactly like a network outage; `ls-remote` on public paths still works). Fix: `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 git -c credential.helper= -c 'credential.helper=!gh auth git-credential' <cmd>`.

**Why:** each cost a debugging round in the Aug 2026 restore/printing sessions.
**How to apply:** prefer these idioms proactively in any zsh/bash-on-macOS scripting here.

Unattended: the daily backup runs `python3 -I ~/.claude/scripts/recall-bench/check.py` (no model, ~1 s; every eval + bench question against `baseline.json`); a drop becomes a backup error in `.errors.log`. After a deliberate ranking change, re-set it with `--update-baseline`. Related: [[brain-audit-loop]].

**A wrong or stale recall becomes a test question, unasked** (Eric corrects a recalled fact, or a newer file contradicts it; Eric will not remember to ask, so the agent does it): append one tab-separated row to `~/.claude/scripts/recall-bench/questions.tsv`: set `miss`, the question as Eric asked it, the file that holds the right answer (path relative to `~/.claude/projects/` or the vault, as the other rows do), and the right answer in one line. Settle the right answer from the source file yourself; ask Eric only if no file settles it. Then run `CSET=miss bash ~/.claude/scripts/recall-bench/run.sh C` (about $0.06 a question) and record the result in `results.md`. Do not tune recall.py on that question without re-running the 30-case eval.

**Why:** PDF principle 5: the setup must prove itself against a fresh default session on tokens, time and correctness, and keep being tuned. Real misses are the best new test questions.

**How to apply:** Run the eval after any ranking change (no model cost); run the bench before changing routing. Pass line: no new misses on Q1-5 vs the default arm.

### DEV/reference_zotero-expert-reference.md

---
name: zotero-expert-reference
description: "Zotero expert reference distilled from zotero.org/support (read 2026-10-13) — collect, organize, search, annotate, cite, sync, back up. Open for any Zotero how-to, troubleshooting, or setup question."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 25cf7597-8d98-41ad-9f32-763c997e5baa
  modified: 2026-10-13T15:26:05.684Z
---

Source: https://www.zotero.org/support/ (read 2026-10-13). Pages read: quick start, adding items, PDF reader, searching, collections and tags, word processor plugins, sync, data directory, attaching files, duplicates, PDF metadata, tips, bibliographies, styles, notes.

## Collect
- Best way to add items: Zotero Connector save button (Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Safari). It pulls metadata and open-access PDFs. Prefer it over manual entry.
- Add by Identifier (toolbar): ISBN, DOI, PubMed ID, arXiv ID, ADS Bibcode. Separate many IDs with spaces, commas, or line breaks.
- Drop a PDF in Zotero: it becomes a standalone attachment and metadata is retrieved automatically. The first few pages go to a Zotero lookup service (Crossref plus DOI/ISBN lookup; no account needed). If that fails: right-click > Create Parent Item (enter DOI/ISBN), or Manual Entry.
- Prefer child attachments under a parent item. Standalone attachments cannot be cited and are not used by My Publications.
- Stored files (default) live in the data directory and Zotero manages them. Linked files (Ctrl/Cmd-drag with modifier, or Attach Link to File) are not synced and do not work in group libraries. Convert with Tools > Manage Attachments.
- Large batches from Google Scholar, ProQuest, or Web of Science: export BibTeX or RIS and import the file. This avoids lockouts.
- Titles: store in sentence case. Zotero converts to title case on output. Journal abbreviations: store with periods.
- Extra field holds custom data. For citing fields Zotero does not support, see the KB article on item types and fields.
- Feeds: RSS subscriptions from journals, to browse and save.

## Organize
- Collections work like playlists. One item can sit in many collections, with no copies made. To move (not copy) between collections: hold Cmd (Mac) or Shift (Win/Linux) while dragging.
- Delete Collection keeps the items. Delete Collection and Items removes both.
- Tags travel between libraries. Collections do not.
- Colored tags (up to 9): press number keys 1-9 to toggle on selected items. Drag items onto a tag in the tag selector to tag them.
- Rename or delete a tag in the tag selector to change it everywhere. Renaming to an existing tag name merges the two.
- Automatic tags (red icon) come from catalog subject headings. Hide them, or delete them library-wide.
- Saved Searches are smart collections that update themselves. Example: Tag is not "read" = a To Read list.
- Special collections: Unfiled Items, Duplicate Items, Trash (30-day default, restorable), My Publications.
- View menu > Show Items from Subcollections.

## Search
- Quick search (Cmd/Ctrl-F) has three modes: Title/Year/Creator; All Fields and Tags; Everything (includes PDF full text). Type a leading quote mark to search only on Enter. This is faster on big libraries.
- Advanced Search (magnifier icon): field filters, Match all or any, Search subcollections, Show only top-level items, Include parent and child items. Wildcard is %, e.g. "W% Shakespeare".
- Saved Advanced Search updates itself. For Boolean logic, save each condition as a saved search, then combine them with a third search: Collection is Condition1 AND Collection is Condition2.
- Full-text index covers PDF, EPUB, HTML, and text files (not .docx). Default limit is 500,000 characters or 100 pages. If an item is missing from "Everything", right-click > Reindex Item. The "Indexed:" field in the right pane shows status.

## Annotate and notes
- PDF reader modes: unlocked (select text, pick a color from the popup) or locked (choose the highlight/underline tool and color; each selection highlights automatically).
- Annotations are stored in the Zotero database, not in the PDF file. External readers will not show them unless you export a PDF with embedded annotations. Adding, rotating, or deleting pages in an external reader breaks annotation positions.
- Get annotations into notes: drag them into the Notes pane, right-click > Add to Note, or right-click the parent item > Add Note from Annotations. Annotation citations link back to the page.
- Child notes attach to an item (Notes tab). Standalone notes come from the New Note button. Notes sync with metadata and do not count against file storage.
- Note editor "..." menu: Show/Hide Annotation Colors, Show/Hide Annotation Citations. Note templates customize annotation output.

## Cite and write
- Word, LibreOffice, and Google Docs plugins ship with Zotero. They insert citations, build the bibliography automatically, and switch styles for the whole document. Reinstall from Cite > Word Processor Plugins in preferences.
- Without a plugin: Quick Copy (drag items into any text field; hold Shift while dragging for in-text citations); Ctrl/Cmd-Shift-C copies the bibliography; Ctrl/Cmd-Shift-A copies a citation; export BibTeX or RIS. The Export pane sets format and HTML markup.
- RTF Scan: write plain text with placeholders, then Zotero finalizes citations and the bibliography.
- Styles use CSL (Citation Style Language). Over 10,000 are in the Zotero Style Repository (zotero.org/styles). For a style error, update Zotero and the style first, then post in the forum titled "Style Error: [Name]".
- Duplicates: Zotero compares title, DOI, and ISBN. Then it checks year (within 1 year) and first-author last name plus first initial. False positives cannot be marked yet. Always merge; do not delete. Merges keep collections and tags, and word-processor citations stay intact. Alt/Option-click selects one item. Merge works on same-type items anywhere in the library.

## Sync and backup
- Data sync is free and unlimited, and covers everything except files. File sync: Zotero Storage (300 MB free, paid tiers; recommended) or WebDAV (not for group libraries).
- Never put the data directory in a cloud-synced folder (Google Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive). It can corrupt the database.
- Default data directory: macOS /Users/<user>/Zotero; Windows C:\Users\<user>\Zotero; Linux ~/Zotero. Find it with Settings > Advanced > Show Data Directory.
- Contents: zotero.sqlite (database), storage/ (one 8-character subfolder per attachment), zotero.sqlite.bak (automatic daily backups), fulltext.sqlite (rebuildable; not backed up). Close Zotero before copying anything. Keep the -wal file with the .sqlite file.
- Backup: use a whole-machine backup such as Time Machine. Do not use export as a backup.
- Restore routes: sync back down; restore a .bak file (rename the current file first); or replace the whole data directory with Zotero closed.
- Replace Online Library (sync reset option) overwrites server data with local data. Use with care.

## Preferences and groups
- General pane: auto-snapshots of web pages, trash period, automatic tags toggle, and the external PDF reader choice.
- Group libraries are shared and separate from personal ones. Duplicate detection runs within each library only.

## Already on this machine (pointers, not copies)
- MCP tools: mcp__zotero__* (search, items_get, collections_*, cite, export, full_text_deep_search, sql, learnings, playbook).
- Skills: pp-zotero-research-library (library search and sync) and sports-science-research-grounding (research answers and batch work). Use them for procedures; this file is only the reference.

## Flint wiring (pointer)
- Flint setup and diagnosis: `~/DEV/Flint/docs/zotero-setup.md` (2026-10-13). Live layer is the bridge in `~/DEV/ZoteroInjestion`, read-only. The Go CLI cache is stale. Fixes need Eric's go-ahead.
